Sun & Site

Geocoding by Nominatim / OpenStreetMap. Searches only run when you press Search or Enter, to stay inside their usage policy.

Keeps the name, coordinates, time zone and elevation together, and adds it to the list above. The time zone is the part searching cannot work out, so it is worth saving once you have it right.

No EPW loaded — using a synthetic clear-sky model (Hottel 1976 / Liu & Jordan 1960). Import an EPW for real climate data.

Held on the server

Tiles come through tile-proxy.php on this site, which holds the key. Nothing secret is in this page, so there is nothing to restrict by domain — the proxy only answers requests from pages on its own host.

The street map, plus the surrounding buildings as volumes: footprints and heights from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API — no key, no account. Heights come from height or building:levels where they are mapped; anything untagged is drawn at 8 m. They cast shadows, and whether they shade the analysis is a switch in Solar Radiation Analysis.

Uses the latitude and longitude above. Tiles are fetched only for this extent — never pre-downloaded — and capped at 6×6.

Any PNG or JPG — a site plan, a survey, an aerial you are licensed to use. Nothing leaves the browser.

Stereographic is the classic printed sun-path chart: the horizon is the outer circle, the zenith the centre, radius = R·tan((90−altitude)/2).

The chart sits on the model centre. Press Place on site and click the spot you want it over — a courtyard, a roof, a street corner.

How heavily the sun paths are drawn. The fine grid stays a hairline and the arcs carry a thin casing, so the chart reads over a map with nothing laid behind it — the site stays visible between the lines.

How to cite

Keeping the notice in the file satisfies the licence; a citation is the scholarly act on top of that.

Report the location, the date and time, the sky model and the analysis settings alongside any figure taken from the tool — an irradiance number without them cannot be checked by anyone reading you.
